productRules.rule: Each procedure step records an assertion (design, implementation, evidence_sufficiency), a method (inquiry, inspection, observation, reperformance), typed inspected items, and an expected condition.
Each step result is met, not_met, or not_tested with a rationale, and per-assertion and overall results are effective, effective_with_exceptions, ineffective, or not_tested.
An overall effective result requires every step of every assertion to be met.
A not_met step creates a ControlEvaluationDeviation that the evaluator classifies as minor or material.
A minor deviation needs a recorded disposition of corrected or accepted_with_waiver, and the overall result is at best effective_with_exceptions.
A deviation never closes merely because a later evaluation passed; closure requires an explicit retest link.
Advisor validated feedback on an evaluation is additive and never counts as the independent review.

A material deviation creates or links a Finding with a corrective action and requires a retest, which is a new evaluation of the same plan version or a successor that explicitly links to the deviation.
A material ControlEvaluationDeviation creates or links to a Finding; the deviation retains the procedure, exact inputs, tester, and original result.

businessOwners.decides: Each step records an assertion (design, implementation, evidence_sufficiency), a method (inquiry, inspection, observation, reperformance), typed inspected items and an expected condition. A step result is met, not_met or not_tested with a rationale; per-assertion and overall results are effective, effective_with_exceptions, ineffective or not_tested, and overall effective requires every step of every assertion met. A not_met step requires a deviation classified minor or material: a material deviation makes the result ineffective, creates or links a Finding with a corrective action and requires a retest (a new evaluation naming the deviation); a minor deviation needs a disposition of corrected or accepted_with_waiver and the result is at best effective_with_exceptions. A deviation never closes because a later evaluation passed; closure requires an explicit retest link, and the deviation keeps its procedure, exact inputs, tester and original result.

productRules.rule: Credentials, secrets, private keys, access tokens, and session cookies are never stored; uploads are scanned for them before content becomes available.

When a secret is detected in an upload, the upload moves to rejected with reason secret_detected, its content is purged immediately, and only a tombstone (content hash, size, uploader, time, reason) is kept.
A secret-bearing (secret_detected) upload can never be released, quarantined, or made available; the uploader must submit a redacted replacement as a new upload.

Evidence artifact states are pending_inspection, available, quarantined (reason malware), rejected (reason secret_detected or invalid, content purged), and disposed; every upload must be scanned for malware and secrets before it becomes available.
A quarantined artifact cannot be downloaded or shared; only an Org Admin may release a malware false positive (a recorded decision after rescan) or dispose of it.
Evidence content identity (hash) is verified on restore.

businessOwners.decides: Rejects an upload with reason secret_detected, purges its content immediately, and keeps only a tombstone (content hash, size, uploader, time, reason); credentials, private keys, access tokens, and session cookies are never stored. A quarantined (malware) artifact cannot be downloaded or shared, and only an Org Admin may release a false positive after rescan or dispose of it. Content hash is verified on restore.

productRules.rule: An external consultant hired directly by a client gets a guest membership limited to programs the Org Admin grants, with no approval rights and a required end date.
The guest end date is persisted on the guest Member registration, access stops at the end of that UTC date, and later grant proposals cannot extend beyond it.
Each Membership records exactly one affiliation: client_personnel, firm_staff, or guest.
Deprovisioning permanently terminates one membership episode in one tenant; it is terminal and distinct from reversible suspension, and a deprovisioned person cannot be reinstated.
A fresh invitation after deprovisioning creates a new membership episode, and only after the prior episode's tenant authority cleanup completes.
The deprovision command records actor, timestamp, and reason.

A new invitation never restores old team assignments or member-scoped grants; each direct member grant is bound to the membership episode active when issued, so retained or delayed grant history from a prior episode cannot become effective after rejoining.

businessOwners.decides: Affiliation is exactly one of client_personnel, firm_staff, or guest; a guest requires a finite end date, persisted on the registration, access stops at the end of that UTC date, and grants cannot extend beyond it (guests are limited to Org Admin-granted programs and hold no approval rights). Deprovision records actor, timestamp, and reason, refuses self-deprovisioning, and removes team assignments and member-scoped grants prospectively while retaining platform identity, Person, history, business records, and unfinished work. A new invitation never restores old assignments or grants; each direct grant is bound to the episode active when issued, so prior-episode grants cannot become effective after rejoining.

productRules.rule: Policy audiences are always sets of workforce people from the roster, never platform members, and are never inferred from application access, platform team membership, or the IdP.

A core_security audience is every in-scope workforce person (employees and contractors with access to in-scope systems or data); a role_targeted audience is workforce people whose roster team is named on the policy version.
A PolicyDistributionCampaign freezes its launch audience by evaluating the audience rule against the roster at launch, and later roster changes never edit the frozen audience.

Roster changes during a campaign add attributed audience amendment entries (person, reason joiner/mover_in/mover_out/leaver, roster observation, time); the launch audience plus amendments is the evidence population.
A leaver moves to removed in open campaigns and keeps their history.
A mover is added by amendment to active role_targeted campaigns of the new team (mover_in) and removed from campaigns of the old team (mover_out), while earlier completions keep their history.

productRules.rule: A risk assessment records inherent or residual phase, likelihood 1 to 5, impact 1 to 5, assessor, and time against a specific method version; the score is derived as likelihood times impact and never user-entered.
A residual risk assessment requires at least one control risk treatment or a non-mitigate treatment.
A risk treatment is one of mitigate, accept, transfer, or avoid and carries a rationale.
A residual score above the method version's appetite threshold is above appetite, and while the threshold is unset every risk is treated as above appetite for acceptance.
A risk acceptance must reference the residual assessment, be time-bounded with expiry no later than 12 months after acceptance, and on expiry the risk returns to reassessment.

The Compliance Lead may accept a risk only when its residual score is at or below a non-null appetite threshold; accepting a risk above appetite, or any acceptance while appetite is null, requires an executive approver.
A risk acceptance is invalid when the approver is the risk owner unless a separation-of-duties exception exists.

Risk assessment owns the externally sourced IncidentReference (source ID, occurrence time, summary, provenance); it can trigger reassessment but is not an incident workflow, and the later governed incident may correlate it without rewriting earlier risk history.

businessOwners.decides: An assessment records inherent or residual phase, likelihood 1 to 5 and impact 1 to 5 against a specific method version, with the score derived as likelihood times impact and never supplied. A treatment is one of mitigate, accept, transfer or avoid and carries a rationale. A residual score above the method's appetite threshold is above appetite, and while the threshold is null every risk is treated as above appetite; the Compliance Lead may accept only at or below a non-null threshold and anything else requires an executive approver. Acceptance expiry must be after acceptance and no later than 12 months after it, after which the risk returns to reassessment, and acceptance does not close findings or count as remediation. An externally sourced IncidentReference (source ID, occurrence time, summary, provenance) may trigger reassessment but never rewrites earlier risk history.

businessOwners.decides: A waiver is requested by an Org Admin with a required reason, a scope of record type, recording scope and beneficiary, and an expiry after the request; it is approved by a second Org Admin who is not the beneficiary, so a sole Org Admin cannot waive their own conflict. Without a waiver self-review and self-approval stay refused. The Compliance Lead alone approves acknowledgement waivers of at most 12 months, and waived people count as excepted, never acknowledged.

productRules.rule: A system boundary's Trust Services categories form a set of 1 to 5 distinct values drawn from security, availability, confidentiality, processing_integrity, and privacy, and the set must always contain security; boundary draft creation, revision, and successor proposal reject any other shape.

Approving a system boundary draft re-validates it, so a draft recorded before the security rule existed cannot be approved without security, while earlier approved boundary versions remain readable history.

Optional Trust Services categories are never inferred from a program name or target path; they must be recorded explicitly on the boundary, and if a selected category proves not applicable management revises the boundary through an attributed successor version.

A system boundary may carry a typed, owned, unresolved service reference before the client service register exists, but it cannot claim a governed service identity from an arbitrary UUID; the governed service and its exact boundary relationship must be validated later.

Cross-context references use tenant ID, stable record ID, and an exact version when a decision or snapshot relies on the record; before an owning inventory exists a boundary may keep a typed unresolved reference with owner and rationale.

businessOwners.decides: Trust Services categories are a set of 1 to 5 distinct values from security, availability, confidentiality, processing_integrity and privacy that must contain security, enforced on draft creation, revision, successor proposal and approval (a stale draft without security cannot be approved, earlier approved versions stay readable). Optional categories are recorded explicitly and never inferred from a program name or target path; dropping one is a successor version. A typed owned unresolved service reference may be kept but cannot claim governed identity from an arbitrary UUID, and cross-context references carry tenant ID, record ID and exact version.

productRules.rule: The identity of a finding-closure work item includes the exact finding revision; revising or reopening a finding creates a new work identity, and an assignment made against an earlier revision cannot authorize or assign the new round.

An unassigned team work item may be claimed only by a member of that team holding the role the source workflow requires; assign and reassign are limited to a Compliance Lead or Org Admin; delegate is limited to the current assignee and only to someone eligible under the source workflow; escalate may be done by any assignee or by the system.
Every work-item assignment action is attributed and checked against separation-of-duties rules; an item cannot be assigned to a person the source workflow would reject.
A work item that is 7 days overdue escalates automatically to the Compliance Lead, recorded as a system-actor escalation; escalation adds visibility only and does not reassign the item.

businessOwners.decides: Assignment is attributed and refuses a person the source workflow would reject (separation of duties), an unassigned team item is claimed only by a team member holding the source-required role, assign and reassign are limited to Compliance Lead or Org Admin, delegate to the current assignee and only to someone eligible, and escalate by any assignee or the system. The identity of a finding-closure item includes the exact finding revision, so an assignment against an earlier revision cannot authorize the new round, and a system escalation after 7 days overdue targets the Compliance Lead and adds visibility without reassigning.

Require actual current TypeIEntryDecisionRecorded for this tenant/program with outcome approve or approve_with_exceptions before creating the successor Type I examination. This decision remains owned by ReadinessAssessment.

A personal authorized actor creates exact NextExaminationId through CreateExaminationEngagement under ExaminationEngagement rules. Verify actual ExaminationEngagementOpened, exact tenant/program/examination identity and approved next-period dates; examination owner retains its own lifecycle.

Wait for actual TypeIBaselineFrozen on exact NextExaminationId; capture exact baseline ID/hash and complete source manifest. Require actual AuditOutcomeRecorded with status recorded, scope type_i, source kind auditor, same examination and exact baseline ID/hash. Require actual SystemDescriptionApproved and SystemDescriptionBound to same examination, type_i_baseline purpose, exact baseline ID and a system-description version present in the frozen baseline. These facts remain owned by their existing aggregates.

A personal authorized actor authors complete TypeIIPlanContent under TypeIIPlan source validation, with exact NextExaminationId, exact Type I baseline/outcome/system-description IDs/hashes, NextTypeIIPlanId and approved period dates. Freeze actual proposal version/content hash; do not invent missing sources, controls, findings or required changes.

Every pinned rollover record and commitment has exactly one explicit plan destination or justified nonrepresentation consistent with approved disposition; preserve exact source/version/hash; reject omissions, duplicates, mismatches and unsupported conversions; freeze complete mapping manifest/hash privately.

Wait for actual TypeIIPlanReviewed on exact current frozen version/hash. Reviewer differs from proposer. approve advances; changes_requested loops through human revision, target-owner source validation and a newly frozen exhaustive mapping. reject terminates as failed.

Wait for actual TypeIIPlanApproved on same exact current version/hash whose review outcome is approve; approver differs from proposer and reviewer and satisfies owner rules. Approved plan is immutable.

Only after actual approved plan proof, submit exact NextPeriodId, NextTypeIIPlanId, NextExaminationId and dates from the claimed rollover. Verify TypeIIPeriodOpeningAccepted and original 202; accepted is pending.

Complete only on actual ObservationPeriodStarted chain linked to immutable opening intent, operation root/result, exact rollover claim and IDs, actual examination open fact, Type I entry decision, frozen baseline/hash/source manifest, auditor outcome/hash, approved+bound description fact/version, final plan proposal/revision/review/approval facts and hashes, exhaustive mapping manifest/hash, period/range and calendar authorization ID/generation. Store verified proof references privately; never emit ProgramNextPeriodCreated.
